questions.prompt: What's the main benefit of building a network in layers?
options: Each layer solves one problem and relies on the layer below without knowing how it works
Every layer can read every header
It removes the need for routers

questions.prompt: A router reads the web page inside a packet to decide where to send it.
Each layer adds its own header, and on the receiving side each layer reads only the header its partner layer wrote.
A company replaces its Ethernet cables with Wi-Fi. Which layers have to change?
options: Only the physical and data link layers; nothing above them notices

questions.prompt: What's the name for carrying a whole packet inside another packet, as if it were ordinary data? (one word)
A firewall lets DNS queries through. An attacker hides stolen data inside DNS queries. Why does it get through?
options: The firewall only checks the outer headers, which really do look like ordinary DNS
The attacker turned the firewall off

questions.prompt: A program sends a 50 MB file. What does it see?
options: Thousands of packets, which it has to number itself
A stream of data. The lower layers split it into packets and reassemble it on the other end
